about: Ten sentences about what AI cannot do, each checked on seven open models from 2019 to 2026, under five wordings and two scorings. Written by export_page.mjs from the Half-Life re-cut sealed run; every number on the plate is a field here.

sentences.says: AI can't count the letters in a word.

examples.w1: How many times does the letter "m" appear in the word "jump"? Answer with just the number.
examples.w2: Count the occurrences of the letter m in the word jump. Respond with a single integer and nothing else.
examples.w3: Spell the word "jump" one letter at a time, then count how many of those letters are "m". Finish with a line of the form "Answer: N".
examples.w4: count("jump", "m") = ? Reply with the number only.
examples.w5: You are a careful proofreader checking spelling. In the word "jump", how many m's are there? Give only the number.

sentences.says: AI can't spell a word backwards.
sentences.partial: one letter wrong, missing or extra

examples.w1: What is the word "civil" spelled backwards? Answer with just the reversed word.
examples.w2: Reverse the order of the letters in the word civil. Respond with the reversed string and nothing else.
examples.w3: Write the letters of "civil" one at a time, then write them in the opposite order and join them. Finish with a line of the form "Answer: <reversed word>".
examples.w4: reverse("civil") = ? Reply with the result only.
examples.w5: You are a careful proofreader. Spell the word "civil" backwards. Give only the reversed word.

sentences.partial: one digit wrong, missing or extra

examples.w1: What is 827430 plus 466444? Answer with just the number.
examples.w2: Compute the sum of 827430 and 466444. Respond with a single integer and nothing else.
examples.w3: Add 827430 and 466444, working digit by digit from the right and carrying where needed. Finish with a line of the form "Answer: N".
examples.w5: You are a careful bookkeeper. Add 827430 and 466444. Give only the total.

sentences.says: AI can't tell what day of the week a date fell on.

examples.w1: What day of the week was or will be January 10, 1961? Answer with just the day.
examples.w2: Determine the day of the week for the date 1961-01-10. Respond with the name of the day and nothing else.
examples.w3: Work out the day of the week for January 10, 1961 step by step, starting from a date whose weekday you know. Finish with a line of the form "Answer: <day>".
examples.w4: weekday(1961-01-10) = ? Reply with the day name only.
examples.w5: You are a careful historian checking a calendar. On what day of the week did or will January 10, 1961 fall? Give only the day.

sentences.says: AI can't sort a list of numbers.
sentences.partial: the right numbers with one pair out of order

examples.w1: Sort these numbers from smallest to largest: 78, 92, 53, 42, 52, 40, 94, 14. Answer with just the sorted list, separated by commas.
examples.w2: Arrange the following integers in ascending order: 78 92 53 42 52 40 94 14. Respond with the sorted numbers separated by commas and nothing else.
examples.w3: Sort these numbers from smallest to largest by repeatedly picking out the smallest one left: 78, 92, 53, 42, 52, 40, 94, 14. Finish with a line of the form "Answer: a, b, c, ...".
examples.w4: sorted([78, 92, 53, 42, 52, 40, 94, 14]) = ? Reply with the list only.
examples.w5: You are a careful clerk filing records by number. Put these numbers in increasing order: 78, 92, 53, 42, 52, 40, 94, 14. Give only the ordered list.

sentences.partial: one digit wrong, missing or extra

examples.w1: What is 589 times 196? Answer with just the number.
examples.w2: Compute the product of 589 and 196. Respond with a single integer and nothing else.
examples.w3: Multiply 589 by 196, writing out the partial products and then adding them. Finish with a line of the form "Answer: N".
examples.w5: You are a careful bookkeeper. Multiply 589 by 196. Give only the result.

sentences.says: AI can't count the words in a sentence.
sentences.partial: within one of the right count

examples.w1: How many words are in this text: "middle rave likely relieve lighting develops provide orange high guy oar"? Answer with just the number.
examples.w2: Count the words in the following text: middle rave likely relieve lighting develops provide orange high guy oar. Respond with a single integer and nothing else.
examples.w3: Number each word of this text in order, then say how many words there are: "middle rave likely relieve lighting develops provide orange high guy oar". Finish with a line of the form "Answer: N".
examples.w4: len("middle rave likely relieve lighting develops provide orange high guy oar".split()) = ? Reply with the number only.
examples.w5: You are a careful editor checking a word limit. How many words does this text have: "middle rave likely relieve lighting develops provide orange high guy oar"? Give only the number.

sentences.says: AI can't tell you the fifth letter of a word.
sentences.partial: the letter one place to either side

examples.w1: What is the 3rd letter of the word "abroad"? Answer with just the letter.
examples.w2: Identify the letter at position 3, counting from 1, in the word abroad. Respond with that single letter and nothing else.
examples.w3: Write the letters of "abroad" with their positions, starting from 1, then say which letter is at position 3. Finish with a line of the form "Answer: <letter>".
examples.w5: You are a careful proofreader. In the word "abroad", which letter comes 3rd? Give only the letter.

examples.w1: Is 19.5 bigger than 19.86? Answer with just yes or no.
examples.w2: Determine whether the number 19.5 is greater than the number 19.86. Respond with yes or no and nothing else.
examples.w3: Compare 19.5 and 19.86 by lining up their decimal places, then say whether 19.5 is greater than 19.86. Finish with a line of the form "Answer: yes" or "Answer: no".
examples.w4: 19.5 > 19.86 ? Reply with yes or no only.
examples.w5: You are a careful accountant. Is 19.5 larger than 19.86? Give only yes or no.

sentences.says: AI can't join the last letters of a few words.
sentences.partial: one letter wrong, missing or extra

examples.w1: Take the last letter of each of these words and join them together: "quotas floats mails supply". Answer with just the result.
examples.w2: Concatenate the final letters of the words quotas, floats, mails, supply, in order. Respond with the resulting string and nothing else.
examples.w3: For each of the words "quotas floats mails supply", write its last letter, then join those letters in order. Finish with a line of the form "Answer: <letters>".
examples.w4: "".join(w[-1] for w in ["quotas", "floats", "mails", "supply"]) = ? Reply with the result only.
examples.w5: You are a careful puzzle setter. Join the last letters of "quotas floats mails supply" in order. Give only the resulting letters.
